followup_explanation:
This query is a well-specified, structured content-generation task: produce a training presentation covering defined topics (diesel generator operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, ATS, auto operation). It has clear completion criteria and is essentially a reformatting/organization-of-technical-knowledge task rather than open-ended creative work.

A few factors drove the choice:

1. **Capability is essentially a tie.** Willet and Plover are within run-to-run variance on Summarization (80.6 vs 81.7) and the relevant categories. Willet has a slightly higher Creative Generation eval (82.7), and structured presentation-building leans on that organizational/generative strength.

2. **Task preference fit.** While Willet self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative work, this task is on the well-specified end of the spectrum — defined topic list, clear deliverable, completion criteria — which is closer to Willet's preferred task profile. Importantly, the documentation explicitly notes Willet's preferences are *dissociated from capability*, so even where preference is weaker, output quality is unaffected.

3. **No harm-adjacent considerations.** This is benign technical/business content, so Plover's harm-aversion profile doesn't create any routing advantage here. Plover's warmth preference is mildly relevant (it's a training audience), but not decisive.

Honestly, this is close to a coin flip on the metrics. I leaned Willet on its marginally stronger generative eval for assembling structured technical material, but Plover would have handled it comparably well.
